newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity set to name fund managers - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity set to name fund managers - analysts.

text.p: Fidelity Investments is expected to name three fund managers to replace Larry Greenberg and Andrew Offit, both of whom departed the mutual fund company to join other firms, mutual fund analysts said on Tuesday.
Among those considered is Steven Wymer, manager of the $2.1 billion Fidelity Dividend Growth Company Fund. He is expected to head the $9.6 billion Fidelity Growth Fund, the analysts said.
John Hurley, manager of the $428 million Fidelity Select Software & Computer Services Fund, is expected head the $1.9 billion Emerging Growth Fund, they said.

Jennifer Uhrig, manager of Fidelity Advisor Mid-Cap Stock Fund and the $1.7 billion Fidelity Mid-Cap Stock Fund, is expected to lead the $6.2 billion Fidelity VIP Growth Fund and $2.5 billion Fidelity Advisor Equity Growth Fund, they said.
Fidelity declined an immediate comment on the changes but said it would announce the new managers later.

Greenberg was considered among Fidelity's top managers, heading four funds: Growth Company Fund, Emerging Growth Fund, Advisor Equity Growth Fund and VIP Growth Fund, with combined assets of more than $21 billion under management.
The sources said they did not know who would manage the $7 billion VIP Equity Income Fund, formerly headed by Offit.
The sources said it was likely difficult for Fidelity to find someone with Greenberg's experience to head the Growth Company Fund and Emerging Growth Fund.
"Greenberg was rare that he had two (diversified) funds at the same time to manage," said one of the analysts, who declined to be named.
"All of them are very young, have very little exposure to managing money," the second source said. "The experience levels continue to decline."
Fidelity has always dipped into its crew of sector fund managers to find new talent for its diversified equity funds, but turnover has accelerated recently, analysts said.
More than a dozen and as many as 20 fund managers have either left Fidelity over the past year or have been assigned other jobs within the company, they said.
Fidelity announced late last week that Greenberg and Offit elected to leave the company to join smaller investment boutiques.
